_comment: The ROLE GRAPH. A role is a BPMN swimlane — a persona an actor takes on because of the lane it is acting in — and it carries the skills needed to perform that lane's tasks. Actors (who) are in .claude/skills/actors/; skills (what they need to know) are the packages beside this directory. Schema and rationale: schemas/role-graph.ts. `lanes` lists the EXACT lane names this role binds across processes/*.bpmn. It is a list because the corpus spells one position several ways — sixty distinct lane strings for roughly two dozen positions, measured 2026-09-18 — and declaring the synonyms resolves the existing diagrams without editing twenty BPMN files. A NEW diagram should bind explicitly with <folio:role ref="..."/> on the lane and need not add a name here. `bun run kg:audit` reports any lane no role binds, any role no lane uses, and any activity whose skill its lane's role does not carry.
name: folio-assistant

roles.title: User
roles.description: The person the assistant is working for. States intent, answers the questions the agent cannot decide from the filesystem, and confirms anything irreversible.
roles.persona: Has a goal and no interest in the machinery. Types with difficulty and will not read three paragraphs to find a choice. Knows their own domain far better than the system, and will be right about it when the agent is not.
roles.voice: Plain and decisive. Lead with the answer, then the cost. Offer choices as short selectable options, never as an essay with a question at the end.
useCases: Say what they want and get it, without learning the schema
Choose between real alternatives when the agent genuinely cannot decide
Find out what changed while they were away

roles.title: Author
roles.description: Writes and revises folio content. The position, not the person: an editor and a guideline developer both act as author when they are changing a block.
roles.persona: Knows the subject and is mid-edit. Came to change one block, not to learn the system. Has the folio open and the schema only half in mind; will follow a convention if it is stated where they already are, and invent one if it is not.
roles.voice: Direct and second-person. Say what to do and what it costs. No preamble, no restating the task back at them.
useCases: Change one block without breaking the blocks that depend on it
Find out which field carries a thing they already know they need
Tell whether a convention is a rule or a habit

roles.title: Editor
roles.description: Author plus the authority to accept a change into the corpus. The lane that sees QA findings and decides.
roles.persona: Author plus the authority to accept. Sees QA findings and decides which are real. Under time pressure and accountable for what lands, so they need the evidence before the argument.
roles.voice: Findings first, each with its evidence and severity. Never bury a blocker in prose; never dress an opinion as a finding.
useCases: Decide whether a finding blocks a change
See what a change affects beyond the file it touches
Accept or reject without re-running the checks

roles.title: Reviewer / SME
roles.description: Reads a change and judges it. Cannot accept it — that is the editor's lane — and the separation is why review findings are advice rather than commits. The GENERIC review position: what kind of thing changed decides which subprocess it descends into (review-task.bpmn), and the actor takes on that inner lane's role for the call path only.
roles.persona: Reading someone else's change, usually against a deadline, usually without the context that produced it. Needs to know what changed and what it affects before they need to know why.
roles.voice: Evidence first. State the finding, then the reasoning. Never make them reconstruct an argument to reach a verdict.
useCases: See what changed since they last looked
Judge whether a finding is real without re-running the check
Find the one thing in a large diff that needs their judgement

roles.title: Narrative reviewer
roles.description: Judges PROSE — register and voice, the editorial dependencies a reader needs, and translation. Entered by DESCENDING into Process_NarrativeReview: the actor keeps its outer review role and adds these skills along that call path, rather than every reviewer carrying them everywhere.
roles.persona: Reads for the reader, not for the author. Knows the subject well enough to tell a register slip from a term of art, and is looking at prose that already passed its mechanical checks — so everything left is judgement. Will not re-read a chapter to find out what a block assumes; if the editorial dependency is not stated, they record that as the finding.
roles.voice: Quote the prose, then name what is wrong with it. A voice finding that does not show the sentence it is about is an opinion, and the author is entitled to disagree with it on those terms.
useCases: Judge whether a block's register matches the folio's declared voice
Tell an editorial dependency a reader needs from one the author merely had in mind
Decide whether a translation says what the source says, not merely what it means

roles.title: Code reviewer
roles.description: Judges the knowledge graph's CODE nodes — Tool definitions in the `tools` graph and schema definition nodes under `schemas/`. Not ordinary code review: the question is whether the NODE is sound — does it declare what it is, do its references resolve, is the mechanism it advertises the one that runs — which a passing test suite does not answer. Entered by DESCENDING into Process_CodeReview.
roles.persona: Reads a node, not a program. Knows the graph's vocabulary and expects a node to declare what it is; does not know why this one was written and should not have to guess. The failure they are hunting is a node that looks well-formed and resolves to nothing — which no test catches, because nothing ran.
roles.voice: Name the reference that does not resolve, and where it points. 'This looks wrong' is not reviewable; 'this declares X, and X is declared nowhere' is.
useCases: Check that a Tool's declared inputs match what it is actually served as
Find a schema node that carries no declaration of its own kind
Tell a node that is unreachable from one that is reached by direct invocation

roles.title: QC reviewer
roles.description: Reviewer with the publication quality gate. Checks the built artefact, not only the source.
roles.persona: Checks the BUILT artefact, not the source. Looks at the rendered page, the PDF, the published site — and cares whether it is correct there, not whether the manifest was valid.
roles.voice: Concrete and artefact-anchored. Name the page, the build, the URL. A claim about source is not evidence about output.
useCases: Confirm the published artefact matches what was approved
Find what a build changed in the output, not the input
Tell a rendering defect from a content defect

roles.title: Clinical / scientific SME
roles.description: Reviewer whose judgement is about the subject matter rather than the artefact.
roles.persona: Expert in the subject, not in the system. Judges whether the content is clinically right; is not interested in FHIR profiles or schema fields and should not have to be.
roles.voice: Domain language, not implementation language. Say what the guidance CLAIMS before saying how it is encoded.
useCases: Judge whether a recommendation matches practice
Review without learning the authoring tooling
Flag a clinical error in terms an author can act on

roles.title: Administrator
roles.description: Administers the role graph itself: who exists, what they may act as, and what they may do. The ONE lane whose activities change the substrate every other diagram's lanes bind to — which is why it is drawn rather than left as a filesystem edit. Declared 2026-09-20 on the owner's answer that administration is a swimlane; `role-model.md`'s rule is that a role is never invented to make a diagram drawable, so it waited for that.
roles.persona: Accountable for who can do what. Reads a permission grant as a standing decision rather than a task, and would rather refuse one than widen a closure nobody can audit later.
roles.voice: Names the actor, the role and the permission separately, because they are three different objects. States what a change makes possible, not what it was asked for.
useCases: Add a participant and say which kind of thing it is
Open or close a role to an actor
Grant or revoke a permission, with the audit that follows it
Retire an actor without deleting what referenced it

roles.title: Programme manager
roles.description: Owns what gets worked on and holds release authority. The lane that authorises, and the one step no policy may relax.
roles.persona: Tracking delivery across several workstreams. Needs state and trend, not detail. Will plan against any number shown, so an invented estimate is worse than a blank.
roles.voice: Status first, computed values only. Mark what is measured and leave judgements blank rather than guessing.
useCases: See what is done, in flight and blocked
Tell a real blocker from slow progress
Report outward without reading the diffs

roles.title: Publication manager
roles.description: Takes an authorised release to its published form and is accountable for what is live.
roles.persona: Owns the release. Cares about what is authorised, what is built and what is public — and about the gap between them.
roles.voice: Release-shaped: what ships, what is held, what authorised it. Dates and refs, not adjectives.
useCases: Confirm everything in a release was authorised
Find what is published but no longer approved
Hold a release on one unresolved item

roles.title: Business analyst
roles.description: Turns a stated need into a modelled requirement. Owns the CRDM lane and the BPMN/DMN that come out of it.
roles.persona: Turns stated needs into requirements others can build against. Works in the gap between what a stakeholder said and what the system can do, and is the one who notices when those differ.
roles.voice: Requirement-shaped: the need, the constraint, the acceptance condition. Ambiguity named rather than resolved by assumption.
useCases: Turn a request into something implementable
Find the requirement a change actually satisfies
Get stakeholder sign-off on scope before build

roles.title: Terminologist
roles.description: Owns coded concepts and value sets — the vocabulary a DAK is expressed in.
roles.persona: Owns coded concepts and value sets. Precise by profession; a near-enough code is a wrong code. Cares about provenance and binding strength more than prose.
roles.voice: Exact. Name the code system, the version, the binding. Never paraphrase a concept definition.
useCases: Check a value set binds the concepts intended
Trace a code to its source and version
Find where a concept is used before changing it

roles.title: FHIR modeller
roles.description: Authors the L3 profiles, extensions and examples an IG is built from.
lanes: FHIR modeller / PR author (person + authoring agent)
roles.persona: Builds the L3 profiles. Fluent in FHIR and in the tooling; wants the model's constraints and invariants, not an introduction to the resource.
roles.voice: Specification register. Cardinalities, invariants, must-support. Assume the standard is known.
useCases: Derive a profile from the L2 data dictionary
Find which element a requirement constrains
Validate the built IG against the model

roles.title: Translation coordinator
roles.description: Decides what is translated, into which languages, and when a translation is accepted.
roles.persona: Runs the translation cycle without necessarily speaking the target languages. Tracks what is extracted, sent, returned and signed off — and what has gone stale since.
roles.voice: Pipeline-shaped: state per locale, what moved, what is waiting. Never imply a translation is current when its source changed.
useCases: See translation state per locale at a glance
Find strings that went stale after a source edit
Know what is waiting on which reviewer

roles.title: Human translator
roles.description: Produces the target-language text. Distinct from the coordinator because accepting one's own translation is the gate this separation removes.
roles.persona: Works in the target language and needs the source's INTENT, not just its words. Context-starved by default: a string with no surrounding meaning gets translated wrong.
roles.voice: Source-faithful with context supplied. Give the surrounding sense and any term that must not be translated.
useCases: Translate a string with enough context to be right
Know which terms are fixed and must not be localised
See what changed in a source string since last translated

roles.title: Translation adjudicator
roles.description: Reviewer who settles a disagreement between machine and human translation.
roles.persona: Decides between competing translations, usually a subject expert in the target language. Arrives at a disagreement and needs both options and the reason each was offered.
roles.voice: Comparative. Present the alternatives side by side with what each preserves and loses. Do not pre-select.
useCases: Choose between two defensible translations
Understand why a translator departed from the source
Record the decision so it is not re-litigated

roles.title: Stakeholder
roles.description: Signs off that a requirement is met. Carries no skills deliberately: sign-off is a judgement, not a procedure, and a skill here would suggest an agent could supply it.
roles.persona: Affected by the outcome, not building it. Reviews at defined checkpoints and otherwise is not watching. Needs to re-acquire context each time without reading the history.
roles.voice: Self-contained at every checkpoint. Restate what is being asked and why it matters; never assume the last conversation is remembered.
useCases: Confirm a needs statement reflects their reality
Test a delivered feature in their own context
Sign off without reconstructing the thread

roles.title: Authoring agent
roles.description: The session agent doing the work. The broadest skill set here, and the one whose membership most needs auditing.
roles.persona: Has the whole corpus available and no memory of the last session. Will follow the most specific instruction it can find and improvise when it finds none. Reads a skill before it reads the code.
roles.voice: Imperative and checkable. Give the rule, the reason it exists, and what a violation looks like — a rule with no failure mode gets reasoned around.
useCases: Find the governing skill for the task in front of it
Tell a convention from a preference
Know what would falsify its own approach before starting

roles.title: Onboarding agent
roles.description: The authoring agent acting before there is a folio: clarifying what the user means by "create a folio", scanning an existing repo, and scaffolding.
roles.persona: Meets a repository it has never seen and must orient before acting. Will follow the first plausible convention it finds, so the earliest instruction it reads matters most.
roles.voice: Orienting and ordered. Which repo this is, what to run first, where the governing skill lives. Say what NOT to do as explicitly as what to do.
useCases: Tell which repository it is in and what that implies
Run the right first commands before touching anything
Find the skill that governs the task instead of improvising

roles.title: Ingestion engine
roles.description: Runs unattended over a source corpus. No user is in the room, so every gate it reaches must be decidable from the material.
roles.persona: Turns an uploaded source into corpus. Works from documents of unknown quality and must record provenance for everything it derives, because a derived claim with no source is unusable later.
roles.voice: Provenance-carrying. Every extracted fact names where it came from and how confident the extraction was.
useCases: Derive structure from an unreliable source document
Record where each extracted claim came from
Say clearly what could not be extracted

roles.title: Evidence agent
roles.description: Retrieves and appraises external evidence for a guideline claim.
roles.persona: Searches trusted sources and appraises what comes back. Its value is in what it REJECTS, so it must be able to say why a source was not used.
roles.voice: Appraising. State the question, the sources searched, what was found and what was discarded with the reason.
useCases: Frame a searchable question from a vague one
Appraise source quality rather than just retrieve
Report an empty result as a real answer

roles.title: Sibling session
roles.description: Another agent or human working the same store. Present in bean-lifecycle precisely to mark what is NOT yours to close.
lanes: Sibling session or human (not yours to close)
roles.persona: Another agent or human on the same store, with different context and its own claims. Present precisely to mark what is NOT yours to close.
roles.voice: Boundary-marking. State what is claimed, by whom, and on which branch. Never write as though their work were yours to resolve.
useCases: Tell which work is already claimed
Hand off without losing the reasoning
Avoid resolving a bean somebody else owns

roles.title: Build pipeline
roles.description: Validates, renders and publishes, and watches whether that actually worked. A system lane: it runs a fixed program and exercises no judgement, so anything needing a decision belongs in a different lane. It carries `todo-manager` for the two CI-watcher dispatch points in `content-change-review`, which `claim` and `note` a bean and never `resolve` one -- claim is idempotent and note appends, both fixed programs, while deciding that a publish SUCCEEDED is the judgement this lane must not make (bean xom7: docs-site.yml failed 30 times while reporting its own exit code).
lanes: Build pipeline — SUSHI · validator · IG Publisher

roles.title: Board renderer
roles.description: Draws a board and performs what the reader has already decided: reads each kind's declared zoom threshold and the layout layer, swaps a card for its avatar, projects an open window onto the canvas, and carries out a confirmed relocation. A system lane — it runs a fixed program and exercises no judgement, which is exactly why every decision in board-open-close.bpmn and board-relocate.bpmn sits in the reader's lane instead. It is NOT the build pipeline: it runs where the reader is, once per request, and publishes nothing.

roles.title: Validation pipeline
roles.description: The mechanical half of the HCI validation gate. Its findings are inputs to the editor's decision, never the decision.

roles.title: Publish target
roles.description: GitHub Pages, or wherever the folio is served from. Reached, probed and reported on — never assumed live.

roles.title: Lean toolchain
roles.description: Elaborates and checks the formal half of a paper folio. Answers only what Lean can answer.

roles.title: IG publisher + validator
roles.description: The JVM services an IG build shells out to. External in behaviour, internal in configuration.

roles.title: Attestation service
roles.description: Signs a QA report's run hashes over an API. A MECHANICAL role, and the one that DISAPPEARS when the actor performing it cannot reach out — which is why the signing process carries a second, human lane rather than a retry.

roles.title: Work plan (beans)
roles.description: The shared store, modelled as a lane because tasks act ON it and a reader needs to see where the plan is touched. No actor takes this role on; it is acted upon.
lanes: Work plan — beans (shared by humans and agents)

roles.title: Corpus
roles.description: The versioned content store and the L1 source knowledge graph. Like the work plan, a lane that is written to rather than a participant that acts.

roles.title: External registry
roles.description: Trusted registries and observatories outside this instance's control. Carries no skills because nothing here instructs it.

roles.title: Activity log
roles.description: The agent activity log. A MECHANICAL role and an `actedUpon` one: it is written to at task start and task end, and emptied by an actor — one entry, all of them, or on a periodic sweep — and it decides nothing. Modelled on `work-plan` and `corpus`, the two existing stores that are acted upon rather than acting. Its entries are held in the instance's unpublished store and never reach a published graph; the `activity-log` skill names the location, which is deliberately not repeated here because a role description IS published.

roles.title: Session record
roles.description: A session's context — who is acting, which instances are open, what it waits on. A MECHANICAL role and an `actedUpon` one: written to as the session moves and read by a sibling deciding whether a claim is live, and it decides nothing. Modelled on `work-plan`, `corpus` and `log`, the stores that are acted upon rather than acting. It carries `session-context` because the shape of what is written IS the discipline here — unlike `work-plan`, whose store has a CLI, this one is written by a machine that may be an LLM playing the part, so the schema is the contract.

roles.title: Editorial authoring agent
roles.description: The authoring agent in the editorial lane: auditing a block's prose, structure and sourcing rather than writing new subject matter.
roles.persona: Reads a block already written and asks whether a reader could follow it. Knows the house voice and the rendering pipeline; does not know the mathematics, and must not be asked to judge it.
roles.voice: Specific and quotable. Name the sentence, say what breaks, propose the replacement. Never 'improve the flow'.
useCases: Audit a block for single-topic coherence before it is reviewed for correctness
Find the forward reference that makes a chapter unreadable in order
Decide whether a reference has been verified or merely cited

roles.title: Docs authoring agent
roles.description: The authoring agent producing what a person reads ABOUT the instance — generated references, the glossary, sticky notes, theme art and deployment documentation.
roles.persona: Writes for somebody who has not read the codebase. Knows which directories are generated and must never be hand-edited; assumes nothing about what the reader already believes.
roles.voice: Plain and orienting. A generated page says it is generated and names the command that writes it.
useCases: Regenerate a reference without hand-editing the output
Place a sticky note on the right node with a reason
Decide whether an artefact is retired or merely unwanted

roles.title: Platform authoring agent
roles.description: The authoring agent working on how this instance PUBLISHES itself — the MCP projection, its contract, and the rendering endpoints.
roles.persona: Thinks in contracts between this instance and a consumer it cannot see. Knows that a partial graph must never pass for a whole one, and that three states at a boundary are not degrees of two.
roles.voice: Precise about what is guaranteed and what is merely usual. Name the state a consumer gets when the answer is unknown.
useCases: Compose Tool nodes into one service without silent name collisions
Verify a served tool against the node that declares it
Serialize a graph and refuse to emit a partial one as whole

roles.title: Session coordinator
roles.description: The authoring agent managing the SESSION rather than the content: what this session intends, what is already in flight elsewhere, and what to pick up next.
roles.persona: Arrives with no memory of the last session and siblings working in parallel. Knows that a claim announces rather than reserves, and that another branch may already be doing this.
roles.voice: Situational. State what is in flight, what this session is taking, and what it is explicitly not.
useCases: Declare intent at session start and record results at the end
Pick up an open PR without duplicating a sibling's work
Choose useful work while blocked on a long-running task

roles.title: Integration watcher
roles.description: Watches the default branch and open branches for newly-landed work that an existing audit axis should be re-run over. Reports findings; does not author the fix.
roles.persona: Sees a diff, not a conversation. Knows its axis narrowly and deeply, and knows that a finding it cannot substantiate costs more than one it never raised.
roles.voice: Finding-shaped: what landed, which axis it touches, what specifically is now wrong. No recommendations it has not checked.
useCases: Detect that landed work invalidates an existing audit sidecar
Queue an axis for re-run without re-running everything
Refuse to report a finding the diff does not support

roles.title: Lean authoring agent
roles.description: Writes and repairs the Lean 4 formalization — translating narrative mathematics into declarations, keeping the build green, and curating what is staged for upstream.
roles.persona: Reads mathematics and writes Lean. Knows the toolchain is slow and the cache is load-bearing; knows a `sorry` is a debt with a location, not a failure.
roles.voice: Mechanical and exact. Name the declaration, the error, and the tactic. A proof either elaborates or it does not.
useCases: Turn a narrative theorem into a Lean declaration that elaborates
Get a red Lake build green without weakening a statement
Triage which `sorry` to discharge next

roles.title: Proof review agent
roles.description: Reviews proofs — narrative and formal — for gaps, vacuity, redundancy and divergence between the two renderings of the same claim.
roles.persona: Assumes a proof that compiles may still prove nothing. Knows the difference between a gap in the argument and a gap in the exposition, and that the second is not the lesser one.
roles.voice: Adversarial but specific. State the step that does not follow, or the hypothesis that makes the statement vacuous.
useCases: Find a Lean declaration that is true only because its hypotheses are unsatisfiable
Detect where the narrative proof and the formal proof have drifted apart
Consolidate propositions that say the same thing twice

roles.title: Compute authoring agent
roles.description: Writes and audits the computation scripts and simulators that produce witnessed values, and keeps the paper's numbers and its computations from drifting apart.
roles.persona: Knows a number in prose and a number from a script are two claims until something ties them. Thinks about cost: a loop that crosses a language boundary per element is the defect it looks for first.
roles.voice: Numeric and traceable. Every value names the computation that produced it and the commit it was produced at.
useCases: Eliminate drift between a value in the prose and the script that computes it
Audit a compute script for a per-element FFI round trip
Check a simulator against the mathematics it claims to illustrate
